items.Sentence: The headworks consist of two micro screens, a Parshall flume, a grit chamber, and weirs for flow control and distribution.
The headworks consist of two micro screens, a Parshall flume, a grit chamber, and weirs for flow control and distribution.
Screened influent flows from the grit chamber to one of two 95-foot diameter conventional primary clarifiers with a design capacity of 15 MGD each.

The Facility also has the option to utilize Chemically-Enhanced Primary Treatment (CEPT), as necessary, during wet weather events. The CEPT uses a coagulant (ferric chloride and an anionic emulsion polymer) to enhance flocculation and coagulation during primary clarification.
Settled primary solids are pumped from the bottom of the clarifiers to the primary anaerobic digesters. The Facility has three primary anaerobic digesters.
The Facility also has two DAFT units which may be utilized to thicken primary solids and WAS.
Each basin now utilizes a diffused air system and has been configured as the Modified Ludzack Ettinger (MLE) activated sludge process.
The secondary clarifiers are of the center-feed, rim-collection type. ... The secondary clarifiers have a total hydraulic capacity of 60 MGD.

Secondary effluent flows from the secondary clarifiers to the secondary effluent diversion box where it is directed to either a cloth-media disk filter system or a conventional deep-bed, dual media filter system. Currently all flow is being filtered using the cloth media filtration system...

Chlorine gas is stored in 1-ton containers and is used to make a concentrated chlorine/water solution to disinfect the filtered secondary effluent. ... A sulfur dioxide/water solution is injected into the secondary effluent flow stream for dechlorination near the outfall building...
Sludge is anaerobically digested and dewatered using a centrifuge. After digestion sludge is dewatered by one of the Facility’s two centrifuges.
Dried biosolids are hauled to a landfill.
The Facility has 13 ponds used for influent flow equalization, emergency storage, and facultative treatment and/or centrifuge centrate management, and solids drying (if necessary).
Biogas is used to fuel hot water boilers for digester heating with natural gas as a secondary fuel.
Excess biogas is combusted at a single conventional flare located east of the CEPT facility.

During the next five years a Pyrolysis system is projected to be installed at the Facility. The Pyrolysis system will be added to the process after the centrifuge. Biosolids will be dried to approximately 80 percent solids.
